Psalms.line: Psalms is Israel's collection of 150 inspired songs and prayers, used in worship to praise, lament, confess, and trust God.
more: It is arranged in five books: Psalms 1–41, 42–72, 73–89, 90–106, and 107–150.
Each book closes with a doxology, and Psalm 150 concludes the whole collection.
David wrote many psalms; others are credited to Asaph, the sons of Korah, Solomon, Moses, Heman, and Ethan.
Its kinds include laments, hymns, thanksgivings, royal psalms, wisdom psalms, and the Songs of Ascents.
Recurring themes include God's kingship, his steadfast love, his law, the coming Messiah, and the righteous and the wicked.
The New Testament quotes the Psalms often, especially as fulfilled in Christ.

1.line: A wisdom psalm contrasting the blessed person who delights in God's law with the wicked, who will perish.
more: The righteous person avoids the counsel and ways of the wicked.
He is like a fruitful tree planted by streams of water.
The wicked are like chaff, but the Lord watches over the way of the righteous.

2.line: A royal psalm in which God laughs at rebellious nations and installs his anointed King on Zion.
more: The nations and their rulers plot against the Lord and his anointed.
God declares the king to be his Son and promises him the nations.
Rulers are warned to serve the Lord and honor the Son.
The New Testament applies this psalm to Jesus.

3.line: David's morning prayer of trust when he fled from his son Absalom, surrounded by many enemies.
more: Many foes claim that God will not rescue him.
David calls the Lord his shield, and he lies down and sleeps in safety.
He asks God to strike his enemies and declares that salvation belongs to the Lord.

4.line: David's evening prayer asking God to answer him, expressing quiet confidence in the Lord.
more: He rebukes those who love vain words and seek after lies.
He urges others to be angry without sinning and to trust the Lord.
God's gladness exceeds abundant harvests, and David lies down in peace and safety.

5.line: David's morning prayer asking God for guidance and protection against deceitful enemies.
more: God does not delight in wickedness, and the boastful cannot stand before him.
By God's steadfast love David will enter his house to worship.
He asks God to hold the wicked guilty and to shelter all who take refuge in him.

6.line: David's lament in severe distress, pleading for mercy and healing as he weeps through the night.
more: He asks God not to rebuke him in anger.
His bones are troubled and his bed is soaked with tears.
He ends confident that the Lord has heard him and his enemies will be ashamed.
It is traditionally counted the first of seven penitential psalms.

7.line: David's plea for justice against false accusers, concerning Cush the Benjaminite, appealing to God as righteous judge.
more: David declares his innocence and invites judgment if he is guilty.
He asks God to rise up and judge the peoples.
The wicked fall into the pit they dug, and David praises the Lord's righteousness.

8.line: David's hymn praising God's majestic name and marveling that he crowned humanity with glory and dominion.
more: God's glory is above the heavens, and he ordains praise from infants.
Considering the vast heavens, David wonders why God cares for human beings.
God made humans rulers over his works; Hebrews applies this to Christ.

9.line: David's thanksgiving for God's righteous judgment of the nations and his care for the oppressed.
more: David praises God for turning back and defeating his enemies.
The Lord reigns forever, judges with justice, and is a stronghold for the oppressed.
He asks God to rise up so the nations know they are only human.
Psalms 9 and 10 together form a loose acrostic.

10.line: A lament asking why God seems distant while the arrogant wicked prey on the helpless.
more: The wicked boast, ignore God, and ambush the innocent.
The psalmist asks God to rise up and break the arm of the wicked.
He ends confident that the Lord is King forever and hears the afflicted.

11.line: David's song of trust, refusing advice to flee because the Lord reigns from heaven and judges justly.
more: Advisers urge him to fly like a bird to the mountains.
The Lord sees all people, tests the righteous, and hates the lover of violence.
He will punish the wicked, and the upright will see his face.

12.line: David's lament over widespread falsehood, contrasting flattering human lips with God's pure and reliable words.
more: The godly seem to have vanished, and people speak with deceit.
The Lord promises to rise up for the poor and needy.
His words are like silver refined seven times.

13.line: David's brief lament asking how long God will hide his face, moving from anguish to trust.
more: He feels forgotten and sorrowful while his enemy prevails.
He asks God to answer lest he sleep the sleep of death.
He ends trusting God's steadfast love and singing of his goodness.

14.line: David's reflection on universal human corruption, beginning with the fool who says there is no God.
more: God looks down from heaven and finds no one who does good.
Evildoers will be terrified because God is with the righteous.
It closes longing for Israel's salvation to come from Zion; Psalm 53 is nearly identical.

15.line: David's wisdom psalm asking who may dwell with the Lord and describing the person of integrity.
more: Such a person walks blamelessly, speaks truth, and does not slander.
He honors those who fear the Lord and keeps his word even when it hurts.
He lends without interest, refuses bribes, and will never be shaken.

16.line: David's song of trust declaring the Lord his only good, his portion, and his security even in death.
more: He delights in God's people and rejects other gods.
The Lord gives him a pleasant inheritance and counsels him.
God will not abandon him to Sheol; Peter and Paul apply this to Christ's resurrection.

17.line: David's prayer for vindication and protection from ruthless enemies, appealing to his own integrity.
more: He asks God to hear his just cause and test his heart.
He prays to be kept as the apple of God's eye.
The wicked are satisfied with this life, but David will be satisfied seeing God's face.

18.line: David's royal thanksgiving after God delivered him from all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.
more: David calls the Lord his rock, fortress, and deliverer.
God descends in storm and earthquake to draw him out of deep waters.
God equips David for battle and gives him victory over nations.
The psalm also appears in 2 Samuel 22.

19.line: David's hymn praising God's glory revealed in the heavens and in his perfect law.
more: The skies proclaim God's work without words, and the sun runs its course.
The law is perfect, sure, right, and more desirable than gold.
David asks forgiveness for hidden faults and that his words and thoughts please God.

20.line: David's royal prayer asking God to grant the king victory in battle.
more: The people pray that God will answer the king and fulfill his plans.
Some trust in chariots and horses, but Israel trusts the Lord's name.
It ends with a plea for the Lord to save the king.

21.line: David's royal thanksgiving for victories God has granted the king, with confidence in future triumphs.
more: The king rejoices in God's strength and has received long life and glory.
He trusts in the steadfast love of the Most High.
God's hand will find and defeat all his enemies.

22.line: David's lament that begins with feeling forsaken by God and ends in worldwide praise for his deliverance.
more: He is mocked, surrounded by enemies, and his hands and feet are pierced.
Enemies divide his garments and cast lots for his clothing.
He vows praise, and all nations and future generations will worship the Lord.
Jesus quoted its opening cry from the cross.

23.line: David's song of trust portraying the Lord as a shepherd who provides, guides, and protects.
more: The Lord leads him to green pastures, still waters, and right paths.
Even in the darkest valley he fears no evil.
God prepares a table before his enemies, and goodness and mercy follow him forever.

24.line: David's processional hymn celebrating the Lord as Creator and as the King of glory entering his gates.
more: The earth and everything in it belong to the Lord.
Only those with clean hands and a pure heart may ascend his hill.
The ancient gates are called to lift up their heads for the King of glory.

25.line: David's acrostic prayer for guidance, forgiveness, and protection, trusting the Lord's steadfast love.
more: He asks God to teach him his paths and remember his mercy.
He confesses the sins of his youth and asks pardon for his great guilt.
The Lord guides the humble and confides in those who fear him.
He ends praying for Israel's redemption from all its troubles.

26.line: David's plea for vindication based on his integrity and his love for God's house.
more: He invites God to test his heart and mind.
He refuses to sit with deceitful and wicked people.
He washes his hands in innocence and will bless the Lord in the assembly.

27.line: David's song of confidence in the Lord as his light and salvation, followed by a plea for help.
more: With God as his stronghold, he fears no army.
His one desire is to dwell in the Lord's house and gaze on his beauty.
He asks God not to forsake him and ends urging others to wait for the Lord.

28.line: David's prayer for help against the wicked, ending in praise because God has heard him.
more: He asks not to be dragged away with evildoers.
He prays that God will repay the wicked for their deeds.
The Lord is his strength and shield and the shepherd of his people.

29.line: David's hymn calling heavenly beings to praise the Lord, whose voice thunders over waters and forests.
more: The Lord's voice breaks cedars, shakes the wilderness, and strips forests bare.
In his temple all who worship cry out, ascribing glory to him.
The Lord sits enthroned as King forever and blesses his people with peace.

30.line: David's thanksgiving, sung at the dedication of the house, praising God for rescuing him from near death.
more: God lifted him from the depths and healed him.
God's anger lasts a moment, but his favor lasts a lifetime.
David had grown self-confident, then cried out when God hid his face.
God turned his mourning into dancing.

31.line: David's prayer for refuge amid enemies and distress, moving from lament to praise for God's goodness.
more: He commits his spirit into God's hands, words Jesus spoke on the cross.
He is grieving, weakened, and scorned by neighbors and plotters.
He trusts that his times are in God's hand.
He ends urging the faithful to be strong and love the Lord.

32.line: David's wisdom psalm describing the blessing of forgiveness after confessing sin he had concealed.
more: While he kept silent, his body wasted away under God's heavy hand.
When he confessed, God forgave the guilt of his sin.
God promises instruction, so people should not be stubborn like a mule.
Paul cites it in Romans on justification by faith.

33.line: A hymn calling the righteous to praise the Lord as Creator and sovereign over the nations.
more: God made the heavens by his word and gathers the seas.
His plans stand forever while the plans of the nations fail.
Armies and horses cannot save, but God watches those who hope in his love.

34.line: David's acrostic thanksgiving after he feigned madness before Abimelech and escaped, inviting others to taste God's goodness.
more: The Lord delivered him from all his fears and troubles.
The angel of the Lord encamps around those who fear him.
He teaches the fear of the Lord: guard the tongue and pursue peace.
The Lord is near the brokenhearted and keeps the bones of the righteous.

35.line: David's plea for God to fight against those who repay his kindness with false accusation and malice.
more: He asks the Lord to take up shield and spear against his attackers.
He had mourned and fasted for these people when they were sick.
He vows to praise God in the great congregation when vindicated.

36.line: David's reflection contrasting the wicked's lack of fear of God with the vast steadfast love of the Lord.
more: The wicked flatter themselves and plot evil on their beds.
God's love reaches the heavens, and his faithfulness reaches the clouds.
In God's light people see light, and David prays for continued protection.

37.line: David's acrostic wisdom psalm urging patient trust in the Lord rather than envy of prospering evildoers.
more: The wicked will soon wither like grass.
Those who delight in the Lord and wait for him will inherit the land.
David has never seen the righteous forsaken.
The Lord upholds the righteous, and their future is peace.

38.line: David's penitential lament describing bodily suffering and isolation that he links to his own sin.
more: God's arrows have struck him, and his iniquities overwhelm him.
Friends stand far off while enemies seek his life.
He stays silent before accusers and waits for the Lord.
He confesses his sin and asks God to hurry to help him.

39.line: David's lament on the brevity of life, praying for understanding and relief from God's discipline.
more: He tried to stay silent, but his distress grew.
Each life is a mere breath, and people heap up wealth in vain.
His hope is in God, and he asks for deliverance from his transgressions.

40.line: David's thanksgiving for past deliverance that turns into a fresh plea for help in present trouble.
more: God drew him from the miry pit and put a new song in his mouth.
God desires an obedient heart more than sacrifice; Hebrews applies this to Christ.
He has proclaimed God's righteousness in the great congregation.
Its closing plea reappears as Psalm 70.

41.line: David's prayer for healing and help against enemies, closing Book One with a doxology.
more: Blessed is the one who considers the poor; the Lord sustains him in sickness.
Enemies hope he will die, and even a close friend has turned against him.
Jesus applied this betrayal by a trusted friend to Judas.
He trusts God to uphold him in his integrity.

42.line: A lament of the sons of Korah, longing for God like a thirsty deer while far from the temple.
more: He remembers leading festive processions to God's house.
Enemies taunt him, asking where his God is.
A refrain asks why his soul is downcast and urges hope in God.
It opens Book Two and shares its refrain with Psalm 43.

43.line: A plea for vindication against deceitful people and for God's light to lead the psalmist back to worship.
more: He asks God why he seems rejected.
He prays for God's light and truth to bring him to the altar.
It repeats the refrain of Psalm 42, urging hope in God.

44.line: A communal lament of the sons of Korah, recalling past victories and protesting a defeat suffered despite faithfulness.
more: God gave the ancestors the land by his power, not by their swords.
Now Israel has been defeated, scattered, and mocked among the nations.
The people insist they have not forgotten God's covenant.
They ask God to awake and redeem them; Paul quotes it in Romans.

45.line: A royal wedding song of the sons of Korah, praising the king and addressing his bride.
more: The king is handsome, victorious, and loves righteousness.
He is addressed as God with an eternal throne; Hebrews applies this to Christ.
The princess is told to forget her people and honor the king.
His sons will be princes, and his name remembered forever.

46.line: A song of the sons of Korah declaring God a refuge and strength amid upheaval in nature and nations.
more: Though the earth shakes and seas roar, God's people will not fear.
A river makes glad the city of God, which shall not be moved.
God ends wars and commands all to be still and know that he is God.

47.line: A hymn of the sons of Korah calling all peoples to praise God as the great King over all the earth.
more: God subdued nations and chose Israel's inheritance.
God has gone up with a shout and the sound of a trumpet.
The princes of the peoples gather as the people of Abraham's God.

48.line: A song of Zion by the sons of Korah, celebrating Jerusalem as the city of God, protected by him.
more: Mount Zion is beautiful, the joy of all the earth.
Kings assembled against it but fled in terror.
Worshipers ponder God's love and are invited to walk around its towers.
This God will guide his people forever.

49.line: A wisdom psalm of the sons of Korah teaching that wealth cannot rescue anyone from death.
more: No one can pay God a ransom for another's life.
Wise and foolish alike die and leave their wealth to others.
God will redeem the psalmist's soul from the power of Sheol.
People should not envy the rich, whose glory does not follow them down.

50.line: A psalm of Asaph portraying God summoning his people to judgment over empty worship and hypocrisy.
more: God shines from Zion and calls heaven and earth as witnesses.
He does not need animal sacrifices, since every creature already belongs to him.
He desires thanksgiving, kept vows, and calling on him in trouble.
He rebukes the wicked who recite his covenant yet hate discipline.

51.line: David's prayer of repentance after the prophet Nathan confronted him over his adultery with Bathsheba.
more: He asks God to blot out his transgressions and wash him clean.
He confesses that he has sinned against God and was sinful from birth.
He asks for a clean heart and a renewed, steadfast spirit.
God desires a broken and contrite heart, and David prays for Zion.

52.line: David's rebuke of Doeg the Edomite, who told Saul that David had come to Ahimelech's house.
more: The boastful man loves evil and uses his tongue like a sharp razor.
God will tear him down and uproot him.
David, like a green olive tree, trusts God's steadfast love forever.

53.line: David's reflection on human corruption, nearly identical to Psalm 14, beginning with the fool who denies God.
more: God looks down and finds no one who does good.
It adds that God scattered the bones of those who besieged his people.
It longs for Israel's salvation to come out of Zion.

54.line: David's prayer for rescue after the Ziphites told Saul that David was hiding among them.
more: He asks God to save him by his name and vindicate him.
Ruthless strangers seek his life without regard for God.
He vows a freewill offering, confident God has delivered him.

55.line: David's lament over oppression and betrayal by a close companion, ending with trust in God.
more: He wishes he had wings like a dove to fly away.
Violence and strife fill the city.
A friend he once worshiped with has broken his covenant.
He urges casting one's burden on the Lord, who sustains the righteous.

56.line: David's prayer of trust when the Philistines seized him in Gath.
more: Enemies twist his words and watch his steps.
A refrain says that, trusting God, he need not fear what mortals can do.
God keeps count of his tossings and stores his tears.
He vows thank offerings for deliverance from death.

57.line: David's prayer for refuge when he fled from Saul into the cave, moving to confident praise.
more: He takes refuge in the shadow of God's wings until danger passes.
He lies among lions whose teeth are spears and arrows.
His heart is steadfast, and he will awaken the dawn with praise.
A refrain asks God to be exalted above the heavens.

58.line: David's denunciation of unjust rulers, asking God to break their power and bring judgment.
more: The rulers devise wrongs, and the wicked go astray from birth.
They are like deaf serpents that ignore the charmer.
He asks God to break their teeth and make them vanish.
The righteous will see that there is a God who judges on earth.

59.line: David's prayer for deliverance when Saul sent men to watch his house in order to kill him.
more: He protests his innocence against bloodthirsty men.
Enemies prowl the city at evening like howling dogs.
God laughs at them, and David asks that they be consumed.
He sings of God as his fortress each morning.

60.line: David's communal lament after a setback during wars with Aram and Edom, appealing to God's promises.
more: God seemed to reject his people and shake the land.
God declares his rule over Shechem, Gilead, Ephraim, Judah, Moab, and Edom.
Human help is worthless, but with God they will do valiantly.
Its second half reappears in Psalm 108.

61.line: David's prayer from the end of the earth, asking God to lead him to the rock higher than himself.
more: God has been his refuge and strong tower.
He longs to dwell in God's tent forever.
He prays for the king's long life and vows daily praise.

62.line: David's song of trust, declaring that his soul waits in silence for God alone.
more: God alone is his rock, salvation, and fortress.
Enemies plot with lies to topple him.
Humans are only a breath, and riches should not be trusted.
Power and steadfast love belong to God, who repays everyone.

63.line: David's song of longing for God, written while he was in the wilderness of Judah.
more: His soul thirsts for God like a dry and weary land.
God's steadfast love is better than life.
He meditates on God through the night and clings to him.
Those who seek his life will fall, but the king will rejoice in God.

64.line: David's prayer for protection from enemies who plot in secret and wound with words.
more: They sharpen tongues like swords and aim bitter words like arrows.
God will shoot his arrow at them, and they will stumble.
All will fear, and the righteous will rejoice in the Lord.

65.line: David's hymn praising God, who forgives, hears prayer, and blesses the land with abundant harvests.
more: Praise awaits God in Zion, and he atones for transgressions.
He stills the roaring seas and the tumult of the peoples.
He waters the earth, and meadows and valleys shout for joy.

66.line: A hymn of praise for God's awesome deeds, moving from communal celebration to personal thanksgiving.
more: All the earth is called to sing the glory of God's name.
He turned the sea into dry land and tested his people through trials.
The psalmist fulfills his vows with burnt offerings.
God heard his prayer because he did not cherish iniquity.

67.line: A communal prayer that God would bless his people so all nations would know his salvation and praise him.
more: It echoes the priestly blessing, asking God's face to shine on them.
God judges the peoples with equity and guides the nations.
The earth has yielded its harvest, a sign of God's blessing.

68.line: David's triumphant hymn celebrating God's march from Sinai to Zion as warrior and protector of the vulnerable.
more: God scatters his enemies and is a father to the fatherless.
He led his people through the wilderness and gave victory over kings.
He ascended on high leading captives; Paul applies this to Christ.
The kingdoms of the earth are called to sing to God.

69.line: David's lament as one sinking in deep waters, suffering reproach for God's sake and asking for rescue.
more: Those who hate him without cause outnumber the hairs of his head.
Zeal for God's house consumes him, and he is given sour wine to drink.
He asks God to judge his persecutors.
He ends vowing praise, which pleases God more than sacrifice.

70.line: David's short, urgent plea for God to hurry to help him, repeating the close of Psalm 40.
more: He asks that those seeking his life be put to shame.
Those who seek God should rejoice and say that God is great.
He is poor and needy and asks God not to delay.

71.line: An older believer's prayer for continued refuge, recalling God's faithfulness since youth.
more: God has been his hope and trust since birth.
Enemies say God has forsaken him, and he asks God not to be far.
He asks not to be abandoned in old age until he declares God's power to the next generation.
He promises to praise God with harp and lyre.

72.line: A royal prayer of Solomon for the king's just and enduring reign, closing Book Two.
more: The king will defend the poor and crush the oppressor.
His dominion will extend from sea to sea, and kings will bring tribute.
All nations will be blessed in him.
A doxology closes Book Two, noting that the prayers of David are ended.

73.line: A wisdom psalm of Asaph, troubled by the prosperity of the wicked until he entered God's sanctuary.
more: He nearly slipped, envying the arrogant who seem free from trouble.
In the sanctuary he understood their sudden end.
He realized that God holds him and is his portion forever.
This psalm opens Book Three.

74.line: A communal lament of Asaph over enemies' destruction of the sanctuary, asking God to act.
more: Enemies have burned the sanctuary, and no prophet remains.
The psalmist recalls God's power in dividing the sea and ordering creation.
He asks God to remember his covenant and defend his own cause.

75.line: A psalm of Asaph thanking God as the judge who sets the time to humble the wicked and exalt the righteous.
more: God holds the earth's pillars steady when it totters.
He warns the boastful not to lift up their horn.
The wicked must drink the cup of God's judgment.

76.line: A song of Asaph celebrating God, who dwells in Zion and shattered the weapons of his enemies.
more: Mighty warriors lay stunned at God's rebuke.
God rises to judge and to save the humble of the earth.
Even human wrath will praise him, and kings should bring him gifts.

77.line: A lament of Asaph that turns from troubled questioning to remembering God's mighty deeds at the exodus.
more: In distress he cannot sleep and asks whether God has rejected him forever.
He resolves to remember God's wonders of old.
God led his people through the sea by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

78.line: A long historical psalm of Asaph recounting Israel's repeated rebellion and God's patient faithfulness, warning the next generation.
more: Parents must teach children God's works so they will not repeat past failures.
Despite the exodus, manna, and water from the rock, Israel tested God.
God rejected Shiloh and Ephraim and chose Judah and Mount Zion.
He chose David to shepherd his people.

79.line: A communal lament of Asaph after the nations defiled the temple and laid Jerusalem in ruins.
more: The bodies of God's servants lie unburied, and neighbors mock.
The people ask God not to hold former iniquities against them.
They pray for help for the glory of God's name.
They vow to give thanks forever.

80.line: A communal lament of Asaph asking the Shepherd of Israel to restore his people.
more: A refrain asks God to make his face shine so they may be saved.
Israel is pictured as a vine brought out of Egypt and planted.
Now its walls are broken down and wild boars ravage it.
They ask God to strengthen the man at his right hand.

81.line: A festival psalm of Asaph calling Israel to worship and recounting God's plea for their obedience.
more: The people sing and blow the trumpet at the new moon and the feast.
God recalls freeing them from slavery and testing them at Meribah.
He wishes Israel would listen, so he could subdue their enemies and feed them.

82.line: A psalm of Asaph in which God judges unjust rulers, called gods, for failing the weak.
more: God stands in the divine council and rebukes partial judgment.
Rulers must defend the poor, fatherless, and needy.
Though called gods, they will die like men; Jesus cited this.
The psalm asks God to rise and judge the earth.

83.line: A communal prayer of Asaph asking God to act against a coalition of nations conspiring to destroy Israel.
more: Edom, Moab, Ammon, Philistia, Tyre, Assyria, and others have allied together.
He asks God to treat them as he did Midian, Sisera, and Jabin.
He prays they will be shamed so that they seek the Lord's name.

84.line: A song of the sons of Korah expressing deep longing for God's dwelling place and the joy of worship there.
more: Even sparrows find a home near God's altars.
Pilgrims on the way to Zion go from strength to strength.
A day in God's courts is better than a thousand elsewhere.
The Lord withholds no good thing from those who walk uprightly.

85.line: A communal prayer of the sons of Korah asking God to revive his people as he restored them before.
more: God once forgave their iniquity and turned from his anger.
They ask him to show steadfast love and grant salvation.
Steadfast love and faithfulness meet, and righteousness and peace kiss.

86.line: David's prayer for mercy and help in trouble, grounded in God's unique greatness and steadfast love.
more: He calls himself poor and needy and asks God to preserve his life.
All nations will come and worship God, who alone is God.
He asks for an undivided heart to fear God's name.
He asks for a sign of favor against insolent men.

87.line: A song of the sons of Korah celebrating Zion as the city where even foreign peoples are counted as born.
more: The Lord loves Zion's gates more than all Jacob's dwellings.
Egypt, Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Cush are registered among those born there.
Singers and dancers say all their springs are in Zion.

88.line: A lament of Heman the Ezrahite, crying out to God from lifelong affliction and nearness to death.
more: He feels counted among those in the pit, cut off from God.
Friends have been taken from him, and he is a horror to them.
He asks whether the dead can praise God.
It ends without resolution, with darkness as his closest companion.

89.line: Ethan the Ezrahite's psalm celebrating God's covenant with David, then lamenting its apparent collapse, closing Book Three.
more: God's steadfast love and faithfulness are praised in heaven and creation.
God promised David an everlasting throne and offspring.
Yet the king's crown is defiled and his enemies rejoice.
The psalmist asks how long and appeals to God's oath.

90.line: A prayer of Moses contrasting God's eternity with human frailty and asking God for wisdom and favor.
more: A thousand years are like a day in God's sight.
Human life is brief, troubled, and under God's wrath because of sin.
He asks God to teach them to number their days.
He asks God to establish the work of their hands; it opens Book Four.

91.line: A song of trust describing the security of those who dwell in the shelter of the Most High.
more: God protects them from snares, plague, and terror by night.
He commands his angels to guard them; Satan quoted this to Jesus.
God promises to rescue, honor, and satisfy the one who loves him.

92.line: A thanksgiving song for the Sabbath, praising God's works and the flourishing of the righteous.
more: It is good to declare God's love in the morning and faithfulness at night.
The wicked sprout like grass but are destroyed forever.
The righteous flourish like palm trees and bear fruit in old age.

93.line: A hymn proclaiming that the Lord reigns, robed in majesty and mightier than the roaring floods.
more: The world is established, and God's throne is from eternity.
The floods lift up their voice, but the Lord on high is mightier.
His decrees are trustworthy, and holiness befits his house.

94.line: A plea for God, the judge of the earth, to repay the proud who crush his people.
more: The wicked kill the widow and assume God does not see.
The one who made the ear and eye surely hears and sees.
Blessed is the one God disciplines and teaches from his law.
When the psalmist's foot slipped, God's steadfast love held him up.

95.line: A call to worship the Lord as great King and Creator, with a warning against hardened hearts.
more: The people are invited to sing, give thanks, and kneel before their Maker.
They are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
God warns them not to harden hearts as at Meribah; Hebrews expounds this.

96.line: A hymn calling all the earth to sing a new song to the Lord, who comes to judge.
more: The gods of the nations are idols, but the Lord made the heavens.
The families of the peoples are called to bring offerings and worship.
Creation rejoices because God will judge the world in righteousness.
Much of it also appears in 1 Chronicles 16.

97.line: A hymn proclaiming the Lord's reign, revealed in fire and lightning, bringing joy to the righteous.
more: Clouds, fire, and lightning surround him, and mountains melt like wax.
Worshipers of idols are put to shame.
God guards his faithful ones, and light dawns for the righteous.

98.line: A hymn calling for a new song because the Lord has made his salvation known to the nations.
more: He has remembered his steadfast love and faithfulness to Israel.
The earth is called to praise with lyre, trumpets, and horn.
Seas, rivers, and hills rejoice before the Lord, who comes to judge.

99.line: A hymn exalting the Lord as holy King, enthroned above the cherubim.
more: A refrain declares that he is holy.
He loves justice and has established equity in Jacob.
Moses, Aaron, and Samuel called on him, and he answered.
He forgave his people yet also avenged their wrongdoings.

100.line: A short thanksgiving hymn calling all the earth to serve the Lord with gladness.
more: The Lord is God, who made his people the sheep of his pasture.
Worshipers enter his gates with thanksgiving and his courts with praise.
The Lord is good, and his love and faithfulness endure forever.

101.line: David's royal pledge to rule with integrity and to remove wickedness from his house and land.
more: He resolves to walk blamelessly and set nothing worthless before him.
He will not tolerate slanderers or the proud.
He will favor the faithful in the land and cut off evildoers.

102.line: A prayer of an afflicted person pouring out his complaint, contrasting his fading life with God's eternal reign.
more: His days vanish like smoke, and he is like a lonely bird.
God will arise and have pity on Zion, and nations will fear him.
The heavens will wear out, but God remains; Hebrews applies this to Christ.

103.line: David's hymn calling his soul to bless the Lord for his forgiveness, compassion, and steadfast love.
more: God forgives iniquity, heals diseases, and redeems life from the pit.
He removes transgressions as far as the east is from the west.
Human days are like grass, but God's love endures.
Angels and all his works are called to bless the Lord.

104.line: A creation hymn praising the Lord for making and sustaining the world and all its creatures.
more: God stretches out the heavens and sets the earth on its foundations.
He provides water, food, and seasons for animals and people.
All creatures look to him and depend on his breath.
The psalmist prays that sinners will vanish and blesses the Lord.

105.line: A historical hymn praising God's faithfulness to his covenant with Abraham, from the patriarchs to the conquest.
more: God protected the patriarchs as they wandered among nations.
He sent Joseph ahead, then Moses and Aaron with plagues on Egypt.
He led Israel out and provided quail, bread from heaven, and water.
He gave them the land so they would keep his laws.

106.line: A historical psalm confessing Israel's persistent rebellion and God's mercy, closing Book Four.
more: Israel forgot God's works at the sea and craved food in the wilderness.
They made a golden calf, joined Baal of Peor, and adopted Canaanite idolatry.
God disciplined them but remembered his covenant.
They pray to be gathered from the nations, and a doxology follows.

107.line: A thanksgiving psalm calling the redeemed to praise God for rescuing people from various kinds of distress.
more: Wanderers, prisoners, the sick, and sailors cried out and were delivered.
Each scene closes with thanks for God's steadfast love and wonderful works.
God turns deserts into pools and lifts up the needy.
It opens Book Five.

108.line: David's song of praise and plea for victory, combining parts of Psalms 57 and 60.
more: His heart is steadfast, and he will awaken the dawn.
God declares his rule over Israel's tribes and neighboring nations.
Human help is worthless, but with God they will do valiantly.

109.line: David's plea for God to judge a slanderous enemy who repaid his love with hatred.
more: He calls for severe judgment on the accuser and his household.
Peter applied part of it to Judas.
He describes himself as poor, needy, and fading like a shadow.
He trusts God, who stands at the right hand of the needy.

110.line: David's royal psalm in which the Lord enthrones David's Lord as King and eternal priest like Melchizedek.
more: The Lord tells David's Lord to sit at his right hand.
He will rule from Zion over his enemies with willing troops.
He will judge the nations and shatter kings.
Jesus and the book of Hebrews apply this psalm to Christ.

111.line: An acrostic hymn praising the Lord's great works, provision, and covenant faithfulness.
more: His works are majestic, and his righteousness endures forever.
He provides food for those who fear him and sent redemption.
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.

112.line: An acrostic wisdom psalm describing the blessings of the person who fears the Lord.
more: His descendants will be mighty and his household prosperous.
He is gracious, generous, and just.
He does not fear bad news, but the wicked are vexed and vanish.

113.line: A hymn praising the Lord, who is exalted above the heavens yet stoops to lift the lowly.
more: His name is praised from the rising of the sun to its setting.
He raises the poor from the dust to sit with princes.
He gives the barren woman a home; it begins the Hallel sung at Passover.

114.line: A hymn recalling the exodus, when sea, river, and mountains reacted to God's presence.
more: Judah became God's sanctuary and Israel his dominion.
The sea fled, the Jordan turned back, and mountains skipped like rams.
The earth trembles before God, who turned rock into springs.

115.line: A hymn giving glory to God's name and contrasting the living Lord with lifeless idols.
more: Idols have mouths, eyes, and ears but cannot speak, see, or hear.
Israel, Aaron's house, and all who fear the Lord are urged to trust him.
The Lord will bless his people, and they will praise him forever.

116.line: A personal thanksgiving for God's rescue from death, with vows to praise him publicly.
more: The snares of death encompassed him, and he called on the Lord.
God delivered his soul from death and his eyes from tears.
The death of his faithful ones is precious to the Lord.
He will lift the cup of salvation and pay his vows in the temple.

117.line: The shortest psalm, calling all nations to praise the Lord.
more: God's steadfast love toward his people is great, and his faithfulness endures forever.
Paul quotes it to show that Gentiles praise God.

118.line: A thanksgiving psalm celebrating God's enduring love and deliverance, sung in procession to the temple.
more: Israel, Aaron's house, and all who fear God declare that his love endures forever.
Surrounded by nations, the psalmist was saved by the Lord's right hand.
The rejected stone has become the cornerstone; Jesus applied this to himself.
Crowds greeted Jesus with its words when he entered Jerusalem.

119.line: The longest psalm, an acrostic celebrating God's word as the source of life, guidance, and delight.
more: Its 22 stanzas each have eight lines beginning with the same Hebrew letter.
Nearly every line names God's word with terms like law, statutes, precepts, and promise.
The psalmist faces affliction and scorn but clings to God's commands.
God's word is a lamp to his feet and a light to his path.

120.line: The first Song of Ascents, a lament of one living among deceitful and hostile people.
more: He asks to be delivered from lying lips and a deceitful tongue.
He has dwelt too long among those who hate peace.
He is for peace, but they are for war.

121.line: A Song of Ascents affirming that the Lord, Maker of heaven and earth, keeps his people.
more: The psalmist lifts his eyes to the hills and finds help from the Lord.
The Lord who keeps Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps.
He will keep their going out and coming in forever.

122.line: David's Song of Ascents expressing joy at going to Jerusalem and praying for its peace.
more: Pilgrims rejoice to stand within Jerusalem's gates.
The tribes go up there to give thanks, and thrones of judgment are set there.
They pray for peace within its walls for the sake of God's house.

123.line: A Song of Ascents in which God's people look to him for mercy amid contempt.
more: Their eyes look to God as servants look to their master's hand.
They have endured much scorn from the proud.
They plead repeatedly for God's mercy.

124.line: David's Song of Ascents thanking God that without the Lord on their side, Israel would have been destroyed.
more: Enemies would have swallowed them alive like a flood.
They escaped like a bird from the fowler's snare.
Their help is in the name of the Lord, Maker of heaven and earth.

125.line: A Song of Ascents declaring that those who trust in the Lord are secure like Mount Zion.
more: As mountains surround Jerusalem, the Lord surrounds his people.
The scepter of wickedness will not rest on the land of the righteous.
It asks God to do good to the upright and ends with peace on Israel.

126.line: A Song of Ascents recalling joy when God restored Zion's fortunes and praying for renewed restoration.
more: Their mouths were filled with laughter, and the nations noticed God's work.
They ask God to restore them like streams in the Negev.
Those who sow in tears will reap with shouts of joy.

127.line: Solomon's Song of Ascents teaching that human labor is futile unless the Lord builds and guards.
more: Rising early and toiling anxiously accomplish nothing without God.
He gives sleep to his beloved.
Children are a heritage from the Lord, like arrows in a warrior's hand.

128.line: A Song of Ascents describing the blessing on the household of one who fears the Lord.
more: He will eat the fruit of his labor.
His wife will be like a fruitful vine and his children like olive shoots.
It closes with blessing from Zion and peace on Israel.

129.line: A Song of Ascents recalling Israel's long affliction and God's deliverance, praying for the defeat of its enemies.
more: Oppressors plowed Israel's back but did not prevail.
The Lord has cut the cords of the wicked.
Those who hate Zion will wither like grass on rooftops.

130.line: A Song of Ascents crying to God from the depths for forgiveness and waiting in hope.
more: If God kept a record of sins, no one could stand.
With him there is forgiveness, so that he may be feared.
The psalmist waits for the Lord more than watchmen wait for morning.
Israel is urged to hope in the Lord, who will redeem them.

131.line: David's short Song of Ascents expressing humble, quiet trust in the Lord.
more: His heart is not proud, and he does not pursue things too great for him.
He has calmed his soul like a weaned child with its mother.
He calls Israel to hope in the Lord forever.

132.line: A Song of Ascents recalling David's devotion to God's dwelling and God's oath to David's dynasty.
more: David vowed not to rest until he found a place for the Lord.
The ark is brought to its resting place in Zion.
God swore to set David's offspring on his throne.
God chose Zion and will make a horn sprout for David.

133.line: David's Song of Ascents celebrating the goodness of unity among God's people.
more: Unity is like precious oil running down Aaron's beard.
It is like the dew of Hermon falling on the mountains of Zion.
There the Lord commanded the blessing of life forevermore.

134.line: The final Song of Ascents, calling the Lord's servants who serve in the temple at night to bless him.
more: The servants lift their hands in the sanctuary and bless the Lord.
It ends with a blessing from the Lord, Maker of heaven and earth.

135.line: A hymn praising the Lord for choosing Israel, ruling creation, and surpassing all idols.
more: God chose Jacob as his treasured possession.
He controls clouds, lightning, and wind.
He struck Egypt's firstborn and defeated kings to give Israel the land.
Idols are lifeless, but Israel blesses the Lord.

136.line: A litany of thanksgiving in which every line ends by declaring that God's steadfast love endures forever.
more: It thanks God as Creator of the heavens, the great lights, and the earth.
It recounts the exodus, the Red Sea crossing, and the wilderness journey.
It recalls victories over Sihon and Og and the gift of the land.
God remembers the lowly and gives food to all flesh.

137.line: A lament of exiles by the rivers of Babylon, mourning Zion and calling for judgment on their oppressors.
more: Captors demanded songs of Zion, and the exiles hung up their lyres.
The psalmist vows never to forget Jerusalem.
He asks God to remember Edom's role and pronounces judgment on Babylon.

138.line: David's wholehearted thanksgiving for God's answer to prayer and his faithful love.
more: He praises God before the gods and bows toward the temple.
All the kings of the earth will praise the Lord.
God regards the lowly and will fulfill his purpose for David.

139.line: David's meditation on God's complete knowledge and presence, ending with a request to be searched.
more: God knows his thoughts, words, and ways.
There is nowhere David can flee from God's presence.
God formed him in the womb and wrote his days in a book.
He rejects the wicked and asks God to lead him in the everlasting way.

140.line: David's prayer for deliverance from violent and slanderous men who set traps for him.
more: Their tongues are sharp, and venom is under their lips.
He asks God to frustrate their plans.
The Lord upholds the cause of the afflicted.

141.line: David's evening prayer for help to resist evil in speech and companionship.
more: He asks that his prayer rise like incense.
He asks God to guard his mouth and keep him from the feasts of evildoers.
He welcomes rebuke from the righteous and asks rescue from traps.

142.line: David's prayer when he was in the cave, crying out as one alone and pursued.
more: No one cares for him, and he has no refuge.
The Lord is his refuge and portion in the land of the living.
He asks release from prison so he can praise God's name.

143.line: David's plea for mercy and guidance, asking God not to enter into judgment with him.
more: No living person is righteous before God.
Enemies have crushed him, and he remembers God's past works.
He stretches out his hands like thirsty ground.
He asks God to teach him his will and lead him on level ground.

144.line: David's royal prayer praising God who trains him for battle and asking rescue, ending with national blessing.
more: God is his rock, fortress, and shield.
Humans are like a breath, so he asks God to come down and rescue him.
He sings a new song to the God who gives victory to kings.
Blessed are the people whose God is the Lord.

145.line: David's acrostic hymn praising God's greatness, goodness, and everlasting kingdom.
more: One generation commends God's works to another.
The Lord is gracious, merciful, slow to anger, and good to all.
His kingdom is everlasting, and he upholds all who fall.
He is near to all who call on him in truth.

146.line: A hymn urging trust in the Lord rather than mortal princes, opening the final five Hallelujah psalms.
more: When rulers die, their plans perish with them.
The Lord made heaven and earth and keeps faith forever.
He frees prisoners, gives sight to the blind, and upholds the widow and orphan.
The Lord will reign forever.

147.line: A hymn praising God for restoring Jerusalem, caring for creation, and giving his word to Israel.
more: He gathers exiles and heals the brokenhearted.
He counts the stars, sends rain, and feeds animals.
He delights in those who fear him, not in the strength of horses.
He has given his statutes to Israel alone.

148.line: A hymn summoning all creation, from the heavens to the earth, to praise the Lord.
more: Angels, sun, moon, and stars praise him because he created them.
Sea creatures, weather, mountains, animals, kings, and peoples join the praise.
God has raised up a horn for his people Israel.

149.line: A hymn calling Israel to praise its King with song and dance and to carry out his judgment on the nations.
more: The Lord takes pleasure in his people and adorns the humble with salvation.
The faithful have high praises of God in their mouths.
With swords in hand, they execute God's written judgment on kings and nations.

150.line: The concluding hymn of Psalms, calling everything that breathes to praise the Lord with every instrument.
more: God is praised in his sanctuary and in his mighty heavens.
He is praised for his mighty deeds and surpassing greatness.
Trumpet, harp, lyre, tambourine, strings, pipe, and cymbals join the praise.
It closes Book Five and the whole book of Psalms.
